claims.text: The phase-transition onset in initially solid FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles is governed by surface-initiated Cu segregation.
The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are compositionally homogeneous.
Heating causes Cu to diffuse preferentially to and become enriched at FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticle surfaces.
Cu has a lower melting point than the other relevant components of the FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Cu enrichment reduces the local melting point at the nanoparticle surface.
Cu-rich surface regions act as nucleation sites for the liquid phase.
Cu segregation creates a discontinuity in interfacial energies that initiates localized premelting.
The resulting liquid-like domains grow and coalesce as temperature rises, driving the transition to full melting.
Particles preconditioned for greater surface Cu enrichment will begin surface premelting at a lower temperature than particles with less surface Cu enrichment.
Cu-rich zones will spatially coincide with the first liquid regions and will expand with increasing temperature.
Homogeneously composed baseline nanoparticles begin melting only near the bulk melting point and show no prior observable surface segregation.
Impurities can alter thermally induced segregation behavior, so impurity effects should be minimized.
Oxidation must be minimized for the proposed Cu-segregation mechanism to govern the transition.
The heating rate must be slow enough to permit sufficient atomic diffusion.
Kinetic constraints and nanoparticle size may affect the temperature threshold and magnitude of Cu-segregation-induced melting-point depression.
High-temperature in situ imaging can directly monitor structural evolution in metallic nanoparticle systems.
The controlled comparison is between standard FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles and otherwise comparable nanoparticles preconditioned to enhance surface Cu segregation.
Premelting without preferential Cu segregation, or no premelting-onset difference between Cu-enriched and standard samples, would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.

contradictions.description: The standard starting particles are described as homogeneous, and the mechanism predicts that such particles develop Cu surface segregation during heating; however, the baseline says homogeneous particles melt near the bulk melting point without prior observable segregation. It is unclear whether the baseline is the same standard sample or a separate segregation-suppressed control.
